title: Rupture politics: How the EU and Canada can build “global communities” – European Council on Foreign Relations
gist: Toygür argues the EU should not get stuck on whether Canada becomes an 'associate member' but use the EU-Canada partnership as a template for 'global communities' of like-minded powers. Canada aims to double non-US exports within a decade, and the EU can pair Canadian critical raw materials and energy with European processing, investment, research and defence cooperation.

themes.theme: From associate membership to global communities

insights.claim: European Commission president Ursula von der Leyen floated Canada becoming an EU 'associate member', but member states continue to object to the term while backing more ambitious ties.
insights.speaker: Ilke Toygür
insights.so_what: Formal EU-Canada integration is unlikely; expect substantive sectoral deals instead.
insights.locator: Earlier this year, European Commission president

insights.claim: The EU should treat partnerships like the one with Canada as steps towards 'global communities' that extend ever-closer union beyond Europe to bring together powers worldwide, rather than debating terminology.
insights.speaker: Ilke Toygür
insights.so_what: Points to a widening EU network of trade and security deals beyond its neighbourhood.

insights.claim: Unlike Norway, Iceland and Turkey, which are effectively part of an extended continental project, Canadians prioritise deliverables over format and are not primarily seeking single-market integration or regulatory alignment.
insights.speaker: Ilke Toygür
insights.so_what: EU-Canada ties will be built on project-level deliverables, not regulatory convergence.
insights.quote: Canadians care more about the deliverables than the format.

insights.claim: The EU is not a middle power per se but the world's third biggest economic bloc, giving it the power to build partnerships around the logic of a community.
insights.speaker: Ilke Toygür
insights.so_what: EU market scale is the anchor asset for its partnership strategy.
insights.quote: The EU is not a middle power per se: it is the third biggest economic bloc in the world.
insights.locator: The EU should turn these strands

insights.claim: The EU needs global partners to diversify its economy, secure supply chains and provide public goods including security, climate action and digital sovereignty.
insights.speaker: Ilke Toygür
insights.so_what: Supply-chain diversification remains a policy driver for EU trade deals.

insights.claim: Despite pervasive European defeatism, the author finds the EU is still seen favourably in countries such as India, Brazil, South Africa, Japan and South Korea as an imperfect defender of the rules-based order and the only other powerful economy that may set rules.
insights.speaker: Ilke Toygür
insights.so_what: EU soft power supports its ability to sign trade and standards agreements.

insights.claim: Mark Carney describes the EU as integral to his idea of a middle power alliance balancing US-China competition, and the author argues the EU is central to making it work.
insights.speaker: Ilke Toygür
insights.so_what: A middle-power bloc could reshape trade flows away from US/China dependence.
insights.locator: But the bloc can indeed play

insights.claim: The EU's outward turn runs on two streams: free trade agreements, including recent deals with India and Mercosur, and security and defence partnerships signed with 12 countries since 2022, including Canada, Britain and Norway.
insights.speaker: Ilke Toygür
insights.so_what: Expanding EU FTA and defence-partnership network widens market access for European exporters and defence firms.

themes.theme: Canada's diversification away from the US

insights.claim: Canada's turn towards Europe is part of a sovereignty drive to reorient its economy, as both government and society have concluded that excessive dependency on the United States is dangerous.
insights.speaker: Ilke Toygür
insights.so_what: Structural shift in Canadian trade policy away from US concentration.

insights.claim: Ottawa's stated ambition is to double exports to markets outside the United States over the next decade, and seeks more investment in strategic industries including energy and critical raw materials.
insights.speaker: Ilke Toygür
insights.so_what: Implies growing Canadian commodity and energy flows to Europe and Asia over 10 years.
insights.quote: Its stated ambition is to double exports to markets outside the United States over the next decade.

themes.theme: Critical minerals and joint value chains

insights.claim: EU ambitions in climate, digital sovereignty and defence all depend on secure supplies of critical raw materials, energy and industrial capacity, for which the EU sees Canada as a source.
insights.speaker: Ilke Toygür
insights.so_what: Supports demand for Canadian critical minerals and energy projects with European offtake.

insights.claim: The opportunity is to build joint value chains in which Canadian critical raw materials are processed into products with European investment and manufacturing, rather than a relationship confined to shipping raw materials.
insights.speaker: Ilke Toygür
insights.so_what: Look for EU-Canada joint investments in mineral processing, clean energy and defence production.
insights.locator: The opportunity is to build value chains

insights.claim: The EU-Canada summit agenda covers critical raw materials, energy, connectivity, digital trade, youth mobility and research, and both sides have pledged to look at upgrading CETA to include digital trade.
insights.speaker: Ilke Toygür
insights.so_what: CETA digital-trade upgrade would matter for cross-Atlantic tech and services firms.
insights.locator: The EU-Canada summit is set to focus

insights.claim: Canada became the first non-European country to participate in the EU's SAFE defence procurement instrument, following a 2025 Strategic Partnership Agreement and Security and Defence Partnership.
insights.speaker: Ilke Toygür
insights.so_what: Opens EU defence procurement to Canadian defence-industrial firms.
insights.locator: Some of the pieces are already in place

insights.claim: Canada joined Pillar II of Horizon Europe in 2024, and a leaked summit declaration suggests it will start negotiating participation in Erasmus+.
insights.speaker: Ilke Toygür
insights.so_what: Deepening research integration supports joint tech development.

insights.claim: The author proposes joint investment routes in mineral extraction and processing, clean energy and defence production, regular top-level political meetings and a joint business council to track delivery, without first settling the legal meaning of 'associate membership'.
insights.speaker: Ilke Toygür
insights.so_what: A business council would create a channel for corporate input into EU-Canada investment.
